The reactant is ((2,2-dimethylbut-3-en-1-yl)oxy)benzene, which has the structure Ph–O–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH=CH₂. Under acidic conditions with HBr, the alkene is protonated to generate a carbocation. Markovnikov addition of H⁺ gives the secondary carbocation at C3: Ph–O–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–⁺CH–CH₃. This carbocation can undergo intramolecular Friedel–Crafts alkylation at the ortho position of the activated phenyl ring, forming a six-membered cyclic ether (chromane) after rearomatization. The product is 3,3,4-trimethylchromane.

Alternatively, the secondary carbocation can rearrange via a methyl shift from C2 to C3, yielding a more stable tertiary carbocation at C2: Ph–O–CH₂–⁺C(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)₂. Cyclization of this carbocation onto the ortho position forms a five-membered cyclic ether (dihydrobenzofuran). The product is 3-isopropyl-3-methyl-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran.

These two cyclization products correspond exactly to option (B). The other options involve anti-Markovnikov addition (unlikely without peroxides), double-bond migration, or phenol formation, which are not the major pathways under these conditions.

Answer: B
